summary: A canvasser knocks on the door frame instead of ringing, waits, steps back and gives a name.
realLife: A reporter's account says trained canvassers knock rather than ring, wait about half a minute, step back and say who they are and what they are promoting.
sources: Ronald Claiborne Substack, Confessions of a campaign canvasser, undated: https://ronaldclaiborne.substack.com/p/confessions-of-a-campaign-canvasser
inGame: canvass shift record: knock count at the door; second knock if no answer

turns.pulledBy: no answer on the first knock
turns.writesBack: a note on the list and literature left, no scene

turns.turn: A voice answers from inside without opening
turns.writesBack: a short talk through the door
